newsitem.title: FRANCE: REUTERS FRENCH ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST - AUG 14.
newsitem.headline: REUTERS FRENCH ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST - AUG 14.

text.p: News from Reuters and the French press on Advertising, Media & the Internet and Brand-name Products.
PARIS - Publicis, the French advertising agency, is running an unusual campaign for the visit to France next week by Pope John Paul II, a Publicis executive says. (Reuter)

MADRID - Spain's Telefonica has agreed to sell part of its stake in CanalSatelite, a digital television platform owned by France's Canal Plus that competes with its own Via Digital, the national stock market commission says. (Reuter)
PARIS - When French kids head for the beach, their favourite brands follow, invading the 350 beach clubs along the French coast with all kinds of promotions. (Le Parisien)
LONDON - French soccer star Eric Cantona is to play a French nobleman in his first English-speaking film role in the film "Elizabeth I" about the early life of England's 16th century queen. (Reuter)

PARIS - Shares in LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton underperformed on the weak French stockmarket owing to disappointment with its cognac business and newly acquired Duty Free Shoppers, analysts say. (Reuter)

PARIS - Sales in French department stores, hypermarkets, supermarkets and store chains rose 3.9 percent in July from June, compensating for their four percent slide in June, according to the economic service of the Paris chamber of commerce. (La Tribune)

BONN - Apple Computer Inc shouldn't plan on using Europe as a springboard for a comeback in the personal computer business, a market researcher says after releasing second quarter shipment estimates. (Reuter)

PARIS - Sales of multimedia CDs in France more than tripled last year, clocking up 6.7 million sold compared with 2.2 million in 1995, according to a study by specialist institute Electre. It found big differences between the three types of CD -- computer game CDs are the big winners, while CD-ROMs have not won over consumers and video CDs remain marginal. (Les Echos)

PARIS - Famous French chef Joel Robuchon may have signed the contract of the century with Sony, which hopes to sell 430 million francs ($69.6 million) worth of products using his name over the next three years. (Le Figaro)
